newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria, Lebanon to free exchange of local products.
newsitem.headline: Syria, Lebanon to free exchange of local products.

text.p: Syria and Lebanon agreed on Tuesday to gradually lift restrictions on the exchange of local industrial and agricultural products between the two countries, an official statement said.

It said prime ministers Mahmoud Zu'bi of Syria and Rafik al-Hariri of Lebanon decided at talks in Damascus to set up a committee grouping the ministers of economy, finance, industry and agriculture of the two states to implement the decision.

"The decision means that all locally produced goods would be allowed to flow between the two countries freely. The only fees that would be imposed would be low customs duties on the raw materials from which the products are made," one official said.
He said the agreement would improve trade between the two neighbouring countries and that a detailed study on the new procedure would be issued soon.
The official said that Syria agreed to encourage the import of Lebanese-produced bananas and that a price of $85 per tonne was set as a base for customs duties.
Lebanese banana producers had complained that high customs duties kept their product out of the Syrian market.
Lebanese sources said that Damascus responded positively to a request by Beirut to facilitate the flow of Lebanese products which are expected to be shipped to Iraq through Syria.

Lebanon is hoping to take a share of business from Iraq's so-called oil-for-food agreement with the United Nations. The deal allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicines and help offset effects of sanctions imposed shortly after its 1990 invasion of kuwait.
Officials said that Syria agreed to supply electricity to Lebanon's Anjar electricity.
Talking to reporters at the end of the meeting, Zu'bi said there was a "political will in the two sisterly countries to improve ties in all fields".

He said the Damascus meetings discussed issues which would be tackled during a forthcoming session of the Supreme Syrian-Lebanese Council headed by presidents Hafez al-Assad of Syria and Elias Hrawi of Lebanon.
He did not give a date for the meeting.
Hariri said the Tuesday talks centred on how to encourage and activate economic and commercial exchanges between the two countries.
He expressed hope that economic ties would match the "excellent political cooperation".
Syria is the main power broker in Lebanon where it has some 35,000 troops.
